page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Carpels and locules
lines: Bicarpellary — the ovary is made of two carpels.
Syncarpous — the two carpels are fused.
Bilocular — the ovary has two chambers.
Placentation is axile and the placenta is swollen.
steps.why: A technical description is a list of the standard terms, so each term is a separate fact the examiner ticks.
common_mistakes: Writing "two ovaries". There is one ovary made of two carpels.
Writing parietal placentation. Axile placentation goes with a fused, chambered ovary.
steps.memory_tip: Two carpels, joined, two chambers: bicarpellary, syncarpous, bilocular.
steps.margin_note: Four short terms, one per line. Do not write sentences.

steps.label: Position and setting
lines: The ovary sits above the other whorls on the
thalamus, so the flower is hypogynous.
The oblique setting of the carpels is a family
steps.why: The oblique ovary is the one feature that separates Solanaceae from other families with a bilocular superior ovary.
common_mistakes: Saying the ovary is inferior. It is superior in Solanaceae.
Leaving out the 45 degrees. The angle is the marked point.
steps.memory_tip: Superior ovary, and the two carpels sit tilted at 45 degrees. That tilt is the family character of Solanaceae.
steps.margin_note: The word "obliquely" plus 45 degrees is the mark. Do not leave it out.

insider_note: The oblique ovary at 45 degrees is the line examiners look for. Write it even if you write nothing else.
